verbalization: Selgantolimod appears to have a dual target relationship with the Pregnancy zone protein, as evidenced by its interaction with two distinct enzymes—Copper chaperone for superoxide dismutase and Triosephosphate isomerase—both of which are targets of the Influenza B virus B/Hong Kong/259/2010 hemagglutinin antigen (MDCK cell derived, propiolactone inactivated). This suggests that Selgantolimod may inhibit the hemagglutinin antigen, which in turn affects these enzymes and ultimately leads to the inhibition of the Pregnancy zone protein. The presence of a consistent and high-scoring pathway across two different targets implies a potential mechanism where Selgantolimod modulates the activity of the hemagglutinin antigen, which is a well-documented viral protein involved in infection and pathogenesis. The mechanism is supported by the observed interaction between Selgantolimod and the hemagglutinin antigen, which is a key component of the influenza virus. The integration of these findings suggests that Selgantolimod may exert its effects through a direct or indirect interaction with the hemagglutinin antigen, thereby influencing the downstream targets and potentially affecting the Pregnancy zone protein.
